comments.note: DatabaseBackupViewModel: DestinationFolder defaults to string.Empty and no UI guard prevents the user from clicking Backup without selecting a folder first. BackupAsync would be called with an empty path, creating a .sql file in the current working directory (or throwing if CWD is non-writable). A simple IsEnabled guard on BackupCommand (e.g., CanExecute returning !string.IsNullOrEmpty(DestinationFolder)) would improve UX.
No observations beyond the above — all AC items pass, structure is clean and consistent with existing service/VM patterns.

summary: Reviewed 5 files: IDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs, DatabaseBackupViewModel.cs, DatabaseBackupView.axaml, DatabaseBackupView.axaml.cs, AvaloniaDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS. Compiled AXAML bindings are correctly applied; event handler lifecycle is leak-free; no sensitive data in ViewModel; injection risk handled upstream in WP-005.

comments.note: Low — A04 (Insecure Design): DatabaseBackupViewModel.cs Backup() method / DatabaseBackupView.axaml Backup button — BackupCommand has no CanExecute guard for empty DestinationFolder. The TextBox in DatabaseBackupView.axaml has IsReadOnly=false, allowing the user to clear it. Invoking Backup with an empty string causes Path.Combine('', outputFileName) to resolve to a relative filename written to the process CWD (typically the app install directory). This could unintentionally write a database dump containing sensitive data to an unexpected, potentially world-readable location. Remediation: add `CanExecute = () => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(DestinationFolder)` to the [RelayCommand] attribute, or bind BackupCommand.CanExecute to a computed property.

Low — A04 (Insecure Design): AvaloniaDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs / DatabaseBackupView.axaml — both Backup and Close buttons are disabled while IsBusy=true ([RelayCommand(IncludeCancelCommand=false)] means no cancel button), and the CancellationToken passed to IDatabaseBackupDialogService.ShowAsync is explicitly not forwarded. If the underlying mysqldump process hangs, the dialog cannot be dismissed normally and no cancellation path exists for the user without OS-level intervention. Remediation: either add a CancelBackupCommand, or re-enable the Close button while IsBusy=true and wire it to cancel the outstanding backup task.

No other security findings — compiled AXAML bindings (x:DataType) prevent reflection-based binding exploits; event handler lifecycle is correct (try/finally unsubscription in AvaloniaDatabaseBackupDialogService); no sensitive data stored in the ViewModel; injection risk is entirely mitigated by MysqlDumpBackupService (reviewed in WP-005).

comments.note: reviewer-applied-fix: Removed redundant `IsReadOnly="False"` attribute from the DestinationFolder TextBox in DatabaseBackupView.axaml. `IsReadOnly` defaults to false on Avalonia TextBox; the explicit attribute was dead noise with no behavioral effect.

reviewer-applied-fix: Increased dialog Window Height from 240 to 280 in AvaloniaDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs. At 240px the ResultMessage TextBlock (which uses TextWrapping=Wrap) could be clipped or push the toolbar off-screen when the message wraps to a second line. 280px provides safe headroom. No test change required — no test asserts on window height.

DatabaseBackupViewModel.cs Backup() — BackupCommand has no CanExecute guard for an empty DestinationFolder. Clicking Backup with an empty path causes BackupAsync to receive an empty string, which results in the dump file being written relative to CWD (or a DirectoryNotFoundException if CWD is non-writable). A `CanExecute = () => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(DestinationFolder)` on the [RelayCommand] attribute would prevent accidental invocations. This is a behavioral change; not applying as Fix-Forward.

DatabaseBackupView.axaml / AvaloniaDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs — both Backup and Close buttons are disabled while IsBusy=true (no cancel path). If mysqldump hangs, the user cannot dismiss the dialog without OS-level intervention. Future improvement: either enable Close while IsBusy and wire it to cancel the outstanding backup task, or add a Cancel button using `[RelayCommand(IncludeCancelCommand = true)]` on the Backup method.

[documentation-forward] IDatabaseBackupDialogService.cs — the `cancellationToken` param XML doc references `VideoIndexer.App.ViewModels.DatabaseBackupViewModel.CloseRequested` by its full concrete name, leaking the implementation mechanism into the interface definition. The doc comment should describe cancellation behaviour abstractly (e.g., 'The token is not currently forwarded to the underlying ShowDialog call') without coupling the interface doc to a specific implementation type.
